I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to reach out to external services like VirusTotal’s API in real‑time. However, I can walk you through exactly what you’d need to do yourself (or put into a script) so you can pull the WHOIS history for **adobe.com**. --- ### How to Get WHOIS Historical Data from VirusTotal | Step | What to Do | |------|------------| | **1️⃣ Build the URL** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}/whois`
For your case:
`https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois` | | **2️⃣ Set up Authentication** | Add an HTTP header:
`Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_API_KEY}`
Your key would be `adobe_key123`. | | **3️⃣ Make the Request** | A simple `GET` will return the most recent WHOIS record. If you want *historical* records, you’ll need to paginate over the results – each page contains one record per time point. | | **4️⃣ Handle Pagination** | Look at the response headers (`x-pagination-next`) or the body field `links.next` to know whether more pages remain. Keep requesting until there’s no next link. | #### Example cURL Command ```bash curl -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "User-Agent: MyApp/1.0" \ -H "X-Apikey: adobe_key123" \ # older VT v2 style "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/adobe.com/whois" ``` *(If you’re using the newer “Bearer” token approach replace `X-Apikey` with `Authorization: Bearer adobe_key123`).* #### Sample Response Structure ```json { "_id": "adobe.com", "data_type": "whois_history", "attributes": { "records": [ { "created_at": "2019-01-15T12:34:56Z", "updated_at": "2019-02-20T08:21:00Z", "raw_data": "... raw WHOIS text ...", "parsed_records": { "registrar": "MarkMonitor Inc.", "registration_date": "1998-10-04", "expiration_date": "2035-09-30", ... } }, /* …more historic snapshots… */ ], "total_count": 42, "page_size": 100, "next_page_token": null } } ``` > **Tip:** Use pagination parameters (`limit`, `offset`, or `after`) to control how many records you receive per request. --- ### Things to Watch Out For | Issue | Why It Matters | Mitigation | |-------|-----------------|-----------| | **Rate Limits** | VirusTotal imposes strict quotas (e.g., 4 requests/minute for free tier). | Cache responses locally; batch requests when possible. | | **Data Volume** | Some domains accumulate dozens/hundreds of WHOIS changes. | Pull only needed fields (`parsed_records.registrar`, `registration_date`, etc.) instead of full `raw_data`. | | **Privacy / Legal** | WHOIS data may include contact emails that are protected under GDPR. | Respect privacy rules—don’t publish private email addresses unless explicitly allowed. | --- ### Quick Script Snippet (Python) Below is a minimal example using `requests`; feel free to adapt it to whatever environment you prefer. ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/" DOMAIN = "adobe.com" API_KEY = "adobe_key123" headers = {"accept": "application/json", "authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"} def fetch_whois(domain): url = f"{BASE_URL}{domain}/whois" while True: resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers) resp.raise_for_status() data = resp.json() for rec in data["data"]["attributes"]["records"]: print(rec["created_at"], rec["parsed_records"].get("registrar")) # Check for next page links = data["data"]["attributes"] next_link = links.get("links", {}).get("next") if not next_link: break url = next_link if __name__ == "__main__": fetch_whois(DOMAIN) ``` This prints each snapshot’s creation timestamp and registrar name. You can extend it to write all details to CSV, database, etc. --- Let me know if you'd like help tailoring this further—for instance, filtering specific fields, handling errors gracefully, or integrating into a larger pipeline!
